options.option_text: Nurse (a nurse uses syringes, not scalpels primarily)
Surgeon (correct: brush is the primary tool of a painter; scalpel is the primary tool of a surgeon ✓)
Doctor (doctor is general; surgeon specifically uses the scalpel)
Hospital (a place, not a person who uses the scalpel)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Tool → Professional who uses it. Brush is the signature tool of a Painter. Scalpel is the signature tool of a Surgeon. Both are the defining tools that identify the profession.

options.option_text: Tenth (November is the 11th month, not the 10th)
Eleventh (correct: January is the 1st month; November is the 11th month ✓)
Twelfth (December is 12th; November is 11th)
Ninth (September is 9th; November is 11th)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Month → Its ordinal position in the calendar. January = 1st month. November = 11th month. (Sept=9, Oct=10, Nov=11, Dec=12.)

options.option_text: Hill (a hill is related in category to mountain, but not the direct opposite)
Trough (correct: mountain:valley = high:low feature; peak:trough = high:low feature — trough is the opposite of peak ✓)
Summit (summit is the same as peak — its synonym, not opposite)
Ridge (a ridge is a connecting high feature, not the opposite of peak)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Elevated feature → Depressed counterpart. Mountain → Valley (elevated landform : low-lying landform). Peak → Trough (highest point : lowest point of a wave or surface). The analogy is about opposite extremes in elevation/position.

options.option_text: Mammal (cobra is not a mammal)
Reptile (correct: frog belongs to class Amphibia; cobra belongs to class Reptilia ✓)
Insect (cobra is not an insect)
Arachnid (arachnids are spiders, scorpions; cobra is a reptile)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Animal → Its biological class. Frog is an Amphibian. Cobra (a snake) is a Reptile. Note: amphibians can live on land and water; reptiles are fully terrestrial/semi-aquatic with scales.

options.option_text: Song (a song is too small — a composer's output equivalent to a book is a larger composition)
Symphony (correct: an author creates a book; a composer creates a symphony/musical composition ✓)
Orchestra (orchestra is the ensemble that performs, not what a composer creates)
Stage (stage is where performances happen, not what a composer creates)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Creator → Created work. Author creates a Book (their primary intellectual output). Composer creates a Symphony (their primary intellectual/artistic output). Both represent major, structured creative works in their respective fields.

options.option_text: Burning (burning is the same as combustion — repeating the first relationship)
Rusting (correct: oxygen supports combustion; water/moisture supports rusting (oxidation of iron) ✓)
Flooding (flooding is caused by excess water but is not what water 'supports' in the same sense as oxygen supports combustion)
Boiling (boiling is a property of water, not a process it causes/supports in the same analogy structure)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Substance → Process it enables/supports. Oxygen is essential for Combustion to occur. Water (moisture) is essential for Rusting (oxidation of iron) to occur. Both are causal enablers of the process named.

options.option_text: Bottle (bottle is a container, not what is measured in litres for the analogy)
Petrol (correct: yard is the unit used to measure fabric; litre is the unit used to measure petrol ✓)
Weight (weight is measured in grams/kg, not litres)
Water tank (a container, not the substance measured)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Unit of measurement → What it measures. Yard is the unit used to measure Fabric (cloth). Litre is the unit used to measure liquid volumes like Petrol. The relationship is unit → typical substance measured in that unit.

options.option_text: Duck (duck is the wrong bird; gaggle refers to geese not ducks)
Goose (correct: a 'pride' is the collective noun for lions; a 'gaggle' is the collective noun for geese ✓)
Crow (a group of crows is called a 'murder', not gaggle)
Swan (a group of swans is called a 'bevy' or 'wedge', not gaggle)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Collective noun → Animal it describes. Pride = group of Lions. Gaggle = group of Geese. Other common collective nouns: pack of wolves, flock of birds, school of fish, colony of ants, pod of whales, murder of crows, parliament of owls.

options.option_text: Temperature (thermometer measures temperature, not barometer)
Atmospheric pressure (correct: clock measures time; barometer measures atmospheric pressure ✓)
Humidity (hygrometer measures humidity)
Rainfall (rain gauge measures rainfall)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Instrument → What it measures. Clock measures Time. Barometer measures Atmospheric pressure. Common instrument pairs for competitive exams: thermometer→temperature, seismograph→earthquakes, anemometer→wind speed, hygrometer→humidity, sphygmomanometer→blood pressure, galvanometer→current.

options.option_text: Pawn (both ace and bishop are specific named pieces/cards; the question is what GAME bishop belongs to)
Chess (correct: ACE is a specific card in card games; BISHOP is a specific piece in Chess ✓)
Cricket (bishop is not related to cricket)
Deck (ace is found in a deck of cards; bishop is not found in a deck)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Relationship: Game piece/card → The game it belongs to. ACE → Card (game / deck). BISHOP → Chess. The ace is a specific card in playing cards; the bishop is a specific piece in chess. The analogy is about the named element and its game.
